D013-D020_h001.question: "Lately, it's just been… a lot. Since I moved away for university five months ago, everything just feels wrong. I try to go to classes, but it's like my body is moving through quicksand; even walking across campus feels like a monumental effort. I’m finding myself in tears almost every day, sometimes for no reason at all, just a sudden welling up of emotion I can't control. I keep thinking about how my parents divorced right after I left, and I can't shake this feeling that somehow, it's all my fault for leaving home. Like if I had stayed, maybe things would be different. I’m not planning anything, but there are days I just wish I wouldn't wake up. It’s hard to focus on my studies, and everything just feels overwhelming. I know it’s been since I started here that all this began, and it's not like I'm having a full-blown depressive episode, but it's definitely affecting everything."
D013-D020_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D013-D020_h002.question: Life at the zoo used to be my calling, but ever since we lost our star gorilla, Bongo, five months ago, it’s like a vital part of me just… emptied out. I feel this persistent hollow inside. It’s hard to put one foot in front of the other sometimes, even just walking between enclosures feels like a chore, and I find myself just moving slower, lagging. I keep replaying the incident, convinced I could have done something differently, feeling this crushing guilt over Bongo’s passing, even though everyone says it wasn't my fault. Sometimes, I’ll be up on the observation deck and get these terrifying urges, like to just jump over the railing, or when I’m crossing the road, I’ll have a sudden impulse to step in front of a car. It’s not like I have a plan, but the thoughts are there. This whole feeling started right after Bongo died, and it’s been really hard to properly do my job since. It’s just so different from how I felt before.
D013-D020_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D013-D020_h003.question: It's been about five months now, ever since my roommate, bless her soul, passed away. We were inseparable, you know, shared everything. Ever since then, I just feel this deep emptiness inside, like a hollow ache where she used to be. I try to busy myself, pacing the halls, wringing my hands, but it doesn't help much. I even feel guilty sometimes, thinking I should have done more, said more, anything to keep her here. It’s silly, I know, but I can’t shake the feeling. I often think, "What's the point of it all?" or "I just want to close my eyes and not wake up." It's not that I have a plan, but the thoughts are there. The nurses keep saying I’m not myself and the activities here just don't bring me joy like they used to. I know I’m not as bad as some folks who can’t even get out of bed, but this sadness just hangs over me like a dark cloud, and it all started right after Martha left.
D013-D020_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D013-D020_h004.question: "It's like I'm just going through the motions, doctor. For the past five months, ever since the layoffs at the firm started – I mean, not that I was directly affected, but seeing my colleagues, my friends, just… let go – it’s like a cloud has settled over everything. I can’t really feel joy, or sadness, or anything much anymore; it’s all just a dull ache. I find myself pacing around the house, picking at my cuticles without even realizing it. My wife asks what's wrong, and I just… can't explain. I keep replaying old conversations, convinced I said or did something wrong, even trivial things, and that somehow I'm to blame for everyone's stress. Sometimes I just wish I wouldn't wake up in the morning, not in a scary way, just… to not have to face another day. It all started right after word got out about the company restructuring. It's really affecting my focus at work, makes it hard to even start a new project. I know I'm not myself, but I also know it doesn't feel like some deep, fundamental brokenness – it’s tied to all this craziness at the firm."
D013-D020_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D013-D020_h005.question: It all started after the investors pulled out five months ago. I’ve just felt… off. It’s been so hard to even get out of bed. Sometimes, I just sit there and cry for no reason, or for every reason. When anyone asks me a question, it feels like my brain is slow-motion; I just can't get the words out. I keep replaying every single mistake I made with the startup, how I should have done things differently, how it's all my fault. It’s like a broken record in my head, just constant self-blame. A few weeks ago, it got so bad I actually started researching ways to… you know. I even wrote a draft letter. I mean, my life feels like a complete failure. Things just haven’t felt right since then, but I can’t tell if it’s depression or just… everything that happened. Even though things are truly terrible right now, I don't feel like I'm completely "diagnosable" with something major. I just can't function like I used to.
D013-D020_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D013-D020_h006.question:
(Sighs heavily) "Well, Doc, it’s been… a couple of months now, maybe a bit more. Ever since the company laid off half the fleet, including my regular co-driver. That whole situation just flipped everything upside down. I can barely sleep, even when I do get a few hours, I wake up feeling like I haven't slept at all. Just exhausted, you know?

"And the sadness, it just hangs over me. Sometimes I think, 'What's the point? I just want to disappear.' Not like I'd actually do anything, but the thoughts are there, recurring. Making decisions? Forget about it. Even picking out what shirt to wear in the morning feels like a monumental task. My wife, bless her heart, she tries, but I just can't seem to shake this. This whole thing with work really got to me, but it's not like I’m completely shut down or anything. It’s just… a heavy weight."
D013-D020_h006.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D013-D020_h007.question: It's been about two months now, and I just can't shake this feeling of sadness. Ever since my clinic closed down due to that unforeseen legal issue, I've felt pretty useless. Even when I get a full night's sleep, I still wake up feeling completely exhausted, like I haven't rested at all. Making even the simplest decisions, like what to eat for dinner or what to wear, feels impossible; I just stare blankly. Honestly, there are days I just think, "I want to die" or "I wish I could just disappear," though I’d never actually do anything like that. It’s not like it was before, when I felt truly hopeless; it’s more like a constant hum of despair after everything fell apart. I know this mood began right after all the trouble with the clinic started, and it’s really interfering with me trying to figure out what to do next.
D013-D020_h007.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D013-D020_h008.question: "It all started about two months ago, right after the divorce was finalized. Everything just feels… foggy now. I just can't shake this dullness, like I'm watching my own life from a distance. The nights are the worst. I keep having these awful nightmares, waking up in a sweat, and then I can't fall back asleep. During the day, it’s like my brain has sprung a leak – I’m constantly forgetting where I put my keys or how to get to familiar places, which is a real problem when you're a taxi driver. I even started looking up ways to just… end it all, just to stop feeling this way. I even wrote a letter, though I haven't mailed it. Everything feels like too much effort, and I've basically stopped taking fares. My ex-wife kept saying I should get help, but I just feel so drained. The worst of it started really soon after she moved out, within three months, but I wouldn’t say I’m completely devastated, just really off. My doctor seems to think it's directly tied to the divorce and isn't a full-blown depression."
D013-D020_h008.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D013-D020_h009.question: It’s been about two months now, and I just feel… off. Ever since the new regulations came in at the zoo, everything’s changed. The extra paperwork, the pressure not to make even the slightest mistake with the animals – it just broke something in me. I find myself tearing up for no reason, sometimes even in front of the chimps, which is definitely not professional. Sleep’s a joke; I wake up every couple of hours and can’t get back to sleep, just lie there staring at the ceiling, my mind racing. My wife says I’m not myself, and she’s right. I can’t even focus on our conversations anymore, let alone reading about new animal care techniques. It's like my brain just can’t hold onto anything. Things got so bad last month, after a particularly rough week at work, that I actually started looking up ways to just... end things. I even wrote a note, but I just couldn't go through with it. It's not like a deep, dark sadness that makes me feel completely empty, but more like I just can't cope with anything since the workload piled up.
D013-D020_h009.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D013-D020_h010.question: It’s been a rough couple of months, ever since my project at work got shut down. I was really invested in that system for identifying vulnerabilities. Ever since then, it's like a dark cloud has just been hanging over me. I wake up at 3 AM most mornings, my mind racing, and then just lie there, unable to get back to sleep. My head feels so foggy, like my thoughts are wading through treacle. It’s hard to focus on new projects; I just feel myself slipping behind. Sometimes, when it gets really bad, I just think, "I wish I wasn't here anymore," or even, "I just want to end it all." I never think about how I would do it, just that overwhelming feeling of wanting it to stop. It's not like the severe depression I’ve heard about, where people can't even get out of bed; I can still function, albeit poorly. It's definitely tied to losing that project though, which happened about two months ago.
D013-D020_h010.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D013-D020_h011.question: It’s been about ten months now, ever since they reassigned me to this isolated station. I just feel… hollow, you know? Like there's nothing inside. I used to love my solitude, but now it’s different. I barely have the energy to do my rounds, let alone tend to my garden or enjoy the little things I used to. I’ve stopped even bothering with the weekly call to my sister; it just seems like too much effort. Every decision feels monumental, even deciding what to cook from my canned supplies. My old station, with the port nearby, offered a bit more interaction, a bit more life. Moving here, away from everything familiar, it really knocked me off kilter. I’m just feeling pretty down, but I wouldn't say I'm completely gone, if that makes sense.
D013-D020_h011.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h012.question: It's been close to ten months now, and I just can't shake this feeling. Ever since the hotel underwent that unexpected management change and I was passed over for the promotion I’d worked so hard for, everything just feels… grey. I’m constantly drained, even after a full night's sleep, and getting out of bed in the morning to face another day at work feels like scaling a mountain. I used to thrive on hitting my targets and seeing my team succeed, but now, even when things go well, I feel absolutely nothing. It’s like my brain is clouded; I forget simple things, like where I left my keys or what I needed to pick up from the store on the way home. It’s really affecting my work – I’m not as sharp as I used to be, and I worry it's noticeable. I know this all started right after the promotion decision, and even though things have settled down a bit at work, I still feel this way, but I don't think it's as severe as when I was completely devastated before.
D013-D020_h012.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h013.question: Lately, everything just feels… heavy. It’s been about ten months now, ever since Mark and I finalized the divorce. I just can't seem to shake this deep sadness. It’s not like I burst into tears all the time, but it's a constant, gloomy weight. Even getting started on a custom piece, something I used to love, feels impossible. My workshop is full of unfinished projects because I just lack any motivation to even pick up a tool. My head feels so foggy, like trying to think through a thick haze. Before, I could design and execute intricate details, but now any complex thought just makes my brain feel tired almost immediately. This has really affected my business; I’m losing commissions, and honestly, I don’t even have the energy to care. It’s not quite what I’ve heard about a full-on depression, but it’s more than just feeling sad.
D013-D020_h013.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h014.question: It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when things started feeling this heavy, but I’d say about ten months ago, right after everything happened with my mother’s illness. Suddenly, I’m just feeling down all the time; it’s more than just sadness. I used to love greeting my students, but now it feels like I'm dragging myself to school, and even then, I'm so drained all the time, no amount of rest helps. I used to be the first one to organize playdates or go out with my husband, but I just don't have the energy or the interest anymore. I’m even forgetting little things at home, like where I put my keys or what I needed to buy at the grocery store. It's affecting my teaching, my marriage, everything. I know it’s connected to all the stress I’ve been under, but it's not like I'm completely unable to function. I can still do the necessities, but the joy is just gone.
D013-D020_h014.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h015.question: It's like I'm just going through the motions. Everything feels so… flat. This all really started about ten months ago, right after they closed down two of our busiest departments and reorganized everything. My team was cut in half, and the pressure just became unbelievable. Before all this, I used to love finding ways to motivate my staff, but now, I don't get any joy out of it – or anything, for that matter. I just feel constantly drained, like I'm dragging myself through the day even after a full night's sleep. And the crying… it just comes out of nowhere. I'll be sitting at my desk, and suddenly, my eyes are tearing up, and I can't stop it. It’s even hard to pick out what to wear in the morning or decide what to have for dinner; it feels like such an insurmountable task. I know it’s affecting my work; I’m usually so sharp, but decisions that used to be easy now feel impossible. I'm just not myself, but I also don't think I'm clinically depressed, if that makes sense.
D013-D020_h015.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h016.question: "To be honest, doctor, things have been pretty rough for about a year and seven months now. It all started after that incident on the job, you know, when I almost lost my client. It was a close call, and ever since then, it just feels like a dark cloud has been hanging over me. Nothing brings me joy anymore. Things I used to love, like hitting the gym or even just a good movie, just feel... flat. I’ll lie in bed for hours, just staring at the ceiling, trying to fall asleep, my mind racing. During the day, I move so slowly, like I’m in a fog. It’s hard to even get going sometimes, and I feel utterly useless, like I failed. I know I’m trained to protect, but after that, I just feel like I can’t do my job right anymore. It’s been about five months since the direct aftermath, but the feeling hasn't lifted. I keep hoping it will, but it just hasn't. I'm afraid I'm not good enough anymore."
D013-D020_h016.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D020_h017.question:
It's been about a year and a half since I got that knee injury, and honestly, things just haven't been right. I'm a gym instructor, you know? My whole life was about being active, pushing myself. Now, it's like a different world. I’ve barely managed to pick myself up since then; it's like my body itself is just slower, like moving through thick mud. When clients compliment me, or I hit a personal best even with the injury, I just... don't feel anything. It's weird, I don't care.

The nights are the worst. I lie awake for hours, just thinking about everything, especially that moment I fell. And then these thoughts hit me, like it’s my fault the gym’s numbers are down, even though I know it’s just the usual seasonal dip. It feels so real, like I’ve somehow cursed everything, which I know sounds insane. I know this all kicked off right after the injury, about a month later, and it’s still lingering, even though the physical recovery is mostly done. It’s not like I’m completely broken, but I’m definitely not myself, not like I used to be.
D013-D020_h017.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D020_h018.question: "It's been almost a year and eight months since… well, since that huge project at work and then my breakup, and I just haven't been myself. I used to be so on top of things, but now, even starting a simple task at the data center feels like pulling teeth. I just lack any drive to get things done, and forget finishing them. My brain feels so slow, and even my body, like, I move sluggishly, like wading through mud. I wake up constantly throughout the night, usually around 2 AM, and just stare at the ceiling, my mind replaying every mistake I’ve ever made. I feel so guilty all the time, even for really small stuff, like if I’m a few minutes late to my shift, I’ll beat myself up about it for hours. It’s hard to explain, but this all really kicked in about two months after everything went south. It’s definitely not like when I’ve felt down before; it’s more manageable, but it’s still messing with my life."
D013-D020_h018.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D020_h019.question: It’s been almost two years since my husband passed, and honestly, things just haven't been right since. I used to love my evenings – a cup of tea, a good book, maybe some knitting. But now, I just… don't care. It’s like all the joy has drained out of things. Even after a full night’s sleep, I wake up feeling just as tired as when I went to bed, sometimes even worse. My body just feels heavy, like it's a real effort to even get around the house, let alone do my daily chores. I catch myself moving so slowly, it's embarrassing. I even feel guilty about everything, like I could have done more for him, or that I’m a burden to my kids now. This all really started not long after his passing, and while I know he's gone, I just can’t seem to get back to myself. I worry because I know it’s been a long time, but I haven't been able to shake it.
D013-D020_h019.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D020_h020.question: It all started about a year and a half ago, right after the divorce was finalized. Before that, things were, well, normal for me. But after she left… I just haven’t been myself. I find myself constantly replaying every little thing, every argument, every minor misstep I made in the marriage. Like that time I forgot her birthday – still haunts me, even though it was years ago. I wake up around 3 AM every single night, and that’s it, my day’s begun, tossing and turning, unable to get back to sleep. And during the day, I just can’t seem to sit still. My hands are always fiddling, or I find myself pacing around the apartment for no reason. It’s affecting my work, too. I used to love driving, meeting new people, but now, even getting into the cab feels like a monumental effort. The desire to go out, to do anything, just isn't there anymore, and I barely make enough to cover rent these days.
D013-D020_h020.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D020_h021.question: I'm so glad I could finally get an appointment. It's been over a year and three months now since things started to go downhill, right after my fiancé called off the wedding. Every day feels like I'm wearing a lead apron – this constant sadness just hangs over me. I’m exhausted not just from crying, but from the nightmares too; it’s always the same dream, where the dress I’m working on falls apart on the bride. Even simple things feel monumental, like choosing between two kinds of fabric for a new design, or even just what to wear in the mornings. It’s paralyzing. A few months ago, I… well, I tried to end it all. I just couldn't see a way out. I know it’s bad, but I don't feel like it’s as severe as what some of my friends have gone through, like they needed hospitalization for months on end. It just feels like everything in my life stopped making sense after he left, and I can't quite get back on track.
D013-D020_h021.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D013-D020_h022.question:
"Thanks for seeing me, Doc. It's been... hell, going on a year and three months now, maybe a little more, since the divorce really hit me. That's when all this started, right after my ex-wife moved out. Before that, I was fine. Now, every night it’s a struggle to even fall asleep; my mind just races. And during the day, it's like my head is in a fog, I can barely think straight enough to sell a car, which is saying something for a guy like me.

Honestly, most of the time I just feel this deep emptiness inside, like there's nothing there at all. It’s hard to put into words, but it’s more than just being sad. Sometimes, I even picture how I'd do it, you know, just end it all – the specific time, place, and how I'd go through with it. It’s not that I want to die, not really, but sometimes it just feels like the only way out of this gray, empty feeling that took over everything once my marriage fell apart. It’s definitely thrown my whole life off track, but I don’t think it crosses into something more serious. It just feels… tied to everything with the divorce."
D013-D020_h022.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D013-D020_h023.question:
It’s been over a year now, about fifteen months since my mom passed away. I feel like I'm stuck in this constant cloud of sadness. I try to put on a brave face for my students, but inside, it's just this heavy, gloomy feeling that never lifts. I also wake up almost every night in a cold sweat from awful nightmares; they're always about losing her again, or something terrible happening to her. It makes sleep feel like a battle rather than a rest.

My focus at school has gone downhill too. During lessons, I find my mind drifting constantly. Even when I’m trying to follow a conversation or mark papers, it's like my brain just can’t hold onto the information. I've even had these really dark thoughts, you know, "I wish I wasn't here anymore" or "I just want it all to end." I’d never act on them, but they’re there, recurring, and they scare me. I know these feelings really kicked in a couple of months after Mom died. They're definitely making it hard to do my job, and honestly, just to live my life. It's like I'm underwater, always.
D013-D020_h023.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D013-D020_h024.question: I’m not really sure why I’m here, to be honest. It’s just… everything feels like too much since my husband's heart attack last year, a little over a year and three months ago now. He's recovered remarkably, thankfully, but that initial scare just… changed everything. I've felt this persistent gloom ever since, like a heavy cloud has settled over me, not a proper depression, but just very down. It's not like I'm having a full-blown depressive episode or anything, I don't think. I find myself sleeping so much, just drifting off at the shop sometimes, which isn't good for business. And I can't concentrate like I used to. Trying to focus on jewel designs or talking to customers feels impossible; my mind just drifts. Sometimes, I even have these sudden, fleeting thoughts, like a quick urge to just step off the curb into traffic. It's scary, but it's not a real plan or anything. I just want to feel normal again.
D013-D020_h024.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D013-D020_h025.question: It’s been over a year now, about fifteen months since the lab restructuring. I’ve just felt… off. I don’t know. I find myself crying at the smallest things, sometimes for no reason at all, and I just can't seem to stop the tears from flowing. I'm so tired all the time, sleeping for twelve hours if I let myself, and still wanting to nap during the day. It’s affecting my work; every decision, even a small choice about what reagents to use, feels monumental. I just freeze up. I know it sounds terrible, but I’ve even thought about how I could just… end it all, specifically on the bridge near my apartment late at night when no one would be around. This all started right after they brought in the new director and changed everything. It’s been rough, but I wouldn't say I feel “depressed” in the deepest sense, just overwhelmed.
D013-D020_h025.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
